children: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL, Financials), the parent of Google, goes into third-quarter earnings with investors focusing less on growth and more on whether its AI expenditure will yield enough return.
Its value multiple has tightened, but the company's 2027 earnings-per-share forecast has grown to around $14.85 from $14.45 during the previous 90 days.
The problem is money coming in. Capital expenditures for the second quarter were $44.9 billion while free cash flow was minus $5.9 billion.
Also, Google Cloud is developing very quickly.
Cloud sales jumped by 82% to $24.8 billion, while operating profit more than quadrupled to $8.8 billion and margin widened to 35.6%.
And the cloud backlog has also hit some $514 billion.
That leaves investors with a simple choice between short-term financial pressure and the prospect of considerably better AI-driven returns later.
Next catalyst is Alphabet's Oct. 28 earnings release and whether management can prove that investment in AI infrastructure is converting into lasting revenue, margins and cash creation.

title: Alphabet's Q3 Could Reframe Its AI Spending Story
